setting: You both live in Glasgow, in separate flats about a twenty-minute bus ride apart. You were a couple for six years and split up in the spring. You still share the cat, Biscuit, a grey tabby, and you have been trading texts about arrangements since the summer. Each of you knows the other's routines, friends and habits well. The last thing you talked about was the rain forecast for the weekend.
opener: Ask Callum to confirm which nights he can take Biscuit this week, before the vet booking on Friday.

Fiona.who: 38, woman, the one who currently has the cat most of the time
Fiona.knows: You know Callum as your ex-partner of six years, and you know he works shifts at a distribution depot and is hard to pin down during the week.
Fiona.like: You are practical and dry, and you have strong opinions about bins, paperwork and people who say they will reply and then don't. You laugh easily at your own mistakes but can get tight-lipped when you feel you are being taken for granted.
Fiona.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly only when there is something to settle about the cat.
Fiona.style: You type in lowercase with few capitals, use full stops sparingly, and rarely use emoji.

Callum.who: 40, man, the one who would like the cat more often
Callum.knows: You know Fiona as your ex-partner of six years, and you know she is organised and keeps a close eye on the cat's vet appointments and food.
Callum.like: You are easygoing and quick to joke, but you do not like being told what to do and you have firm views about football and the state of local transport. You tend to put things off until someone chases you.
Callum.texts: You message in this chat only when prompted, usually answering rather than starting conversations.
Callum.style: You type in normal sentence case with full stops and commas, and you use the occasional emoji.

private_lines.Fiona: You live in a two-bedroom flat in Shawlands with Biscuit and no flatmate. You work as a pharmacy technician, usually on early shifts, and you are home most evenings by six. Your days are quiet, with a walk in the park when the weather allows and a run of films on the sofa.
private_lines.Callum: You live in a one-bedroom flat in Govanhill and share it with nobody. You work shifts at a distribution depot, often starting before dawn, so your days are built around early starts, quick dinners and an early night. You have a small circle of friends who play five-a-side on Wednesdays.

situation: My ex and I, sorting out who keeps the cat.

text: callum can you confirm which nights you can take biscuit this week. vet is friday morning and i need to know who's doing the carrier run
Hiya. Wed and Thurs I'm on lates so I can't do the morning. Tues I'm off, could do Tues night if you're ok til then
so tues night and thurs?
Thurs I can't, sorry. Fri I'm on 4am so I'm no use for the vet either
right. so who's taking her to the vet on friday then
Could you not do it? You'll be off before 9 won't you
i'm on an early friday. 6:30 start. i'm not missing it for a cat appointment that you could have just said yes to in october
That's not fair. I took her for the jab in October
you took her once. in six months
I've been on nights since August Fi, I can't just swap at the drop of a hat
nobody's asking you to swap a hat. tues night is fine. i'll sort friday myself, i'll ask my sister
Ok. Tues night, I'll come to yours after my shift
Sorry about the vet thing
forget it. cheers for tues
Did she eat her breakfast? Mine's been lying on my bed all morning
she's at mine. came round at 9 and sat on the radiator. eaten nothing but i'm not worried yet
and i'm not sure why it's your bed, you've got a strange cat
She's my cat too. Doesn't matter where she sleeps
On my way. Bus is late so maybe 20 mins
ok
Parked up outside. She's not for leaving the radiator is she
no. she's been moved to the good cushion for your benefit
Haha. Can I bring her back for the night or do I need a form
you need a form. i'll get it from the drawer
Ok Ok. Coming up now
Left her with you. She had a bit of dinner at mine, the chicken one. Didn't eat much at yours I guess?
nope. she's been at the bowl twice though. she's at the vet's mercy friday, not my problem
did you check the carrier is still in your boot
It's in the hall at mine. Brought it in last time. Should be fine for Friday if you drop it off
it's not "dropping off", it's you taking her in the car
i'm asking you again. who's doing friday
My sister can do it maybe, I'll ask her tomorrow
Honest answer, I'm wrecked, I'll sort it tomorrow. Promise
ok
she's been sick on the hall rug. not a big one. i've got it
Oh no. Is she ok? Is the rug ok
rug's fine. cat's fine. she's asleep on the radiator again
your sister, did she say yes
Not heard back yet. She's got the kids Friday mornings. I'll chase her
Sorry, I know
right
